name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

/-! ## Kernel operations as data (§58, §60–§75) -/

/-- A kernel operation O1–O16 with its arguments (§60–§75). -/
inductive KernelOp where
  /-- O1 `derive` (§60). -/
  | derive (src : Nat) (region : List Nat) (m : Mode)
  /-- O2 `split` (§61). -/
  | split (src : Nat) (rs : List (List Nat))
  /-- O3 `release` (§62). -/
  | release (a : Nat)
  /-- O4 `transfer` (§63). -/
  | transfer (src dst : Nat)
  /-- O5 `depend` (§64). -/
  | depend (q x : Nat)
  /-- O6 `enterFrame` (§72). -/
  | enter (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape)
  /-- O7 `exitFrame` (§73). -/
  | exit
  /-- O9 `read` (§66). -/
  | read (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  /-- O10 `write` (§67). -/
  | write (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  /-- O11 `writeShared` (§68). -/
  | writeShared (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  /-- O15 `pin` (§74). -/
  | pin (p : Nat)
  /-- O16 `unpin` (§75). -/
  | unpin (p : Nat)
  /-- O12 `endUse` (§69). -/
...

/-- The base frame 0 is never removed from the stack of a reachable state (§39). -/
theorem reachable_base_mem {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} (h : Reachable k statics s) :
    0 ∈ s.F :=
  List.mem_of_getLast? (reachable_base h)

/-! ## Preservation by every step except `transfer` (§57, §58) -/

/-- Every operation other than `transfer` preserves `KInv` (§57) from its `ok` outcome, under
`DDSound` (§80, used by `split`, §61). -/
theorem op_preserves {k : K} {op : KernelOp} {s s' : S3} (hdd : DDSound k) (hinv : KInv s)
    (h : op.Step k s (.ok s')) (hnt : ∀ src dst, op ≠ .transfer src dst) : KInv s' := by
  cases op with
  | derive => exact derive_preserves hinv h
  | split => exact split_preserves hdd hinv h
  | release => exact release_preserves hinv h
  | transfer src dst => exact absurd rfl (hnt src dst)
  | depend => exact depend_preserves hinv h
  | enter => exact enter_preserves hinv h
  | exit => exact exit_preserves hinv h
  | read => exact read_preserves hinv h
  | write => exact write_preserves hinv h
  | writeShared => exact writeShared_preserves hinv h
  | pin => exact pin_preserves hinv h
  | unpin => exact unpin_preserves hinv h
  | endUse => exact endUse_preserves hinv h
  | free => exact free_preserves hinv h
  | alloc => exact alloc_preserves hinv h
  | store => exact store_preserves hinv h

/-- Every operation, `transfer` included, preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40,
§49.7; not a clause of §57) from a state satisfying `KInv` (§57) and `KAux` to its `ok`
outcome. -/
theorem op_preserves_kAux {k : K} {op : KernelOp} {s s' : S3} (hinv : KInv s) (haux : KAux s)
    (h : op.Step k s (.ok s')) : KAux s' := by
  cases op with
  | derive => exact derive_preserves_rootHeldConv haux h
  | split => exact split_preserves_rootHeldConv haux h
  | release => exact release_preserves_rootHeldConv haux h
  | transfer => exact transfer_preserves_kAux haux h
  | depend => exact depend_preserves_rootHeldConv haux h
  | enter => exact enter_preserves_kAux hinv haux h
  | exit => exact exit_preserves_kAux haux h
  | read => exact read_preserves_kAux haux h
  | write => exact write_preserves_kAux haux h
  | writeShared => exact writeShared_preserves_kAux haux h
  | pin => exact pin_preserves_kAux haux h
  | unpin => exact unpin_preserves_kAux haux h
  | endUse => exact endUse_preserves_kAux haux h
  | free => exact free_preserves_kAux haux h
  | alloc => exact alloc_preserves_kAux hinv haux h
  | store => exact store_preserves_rootHeldConv haux h

/-- Every kernel step from a state satisfying `KInv` (§57) under `DDSound` (§80) either preserves
`KInv` or is an accepted `transfer` (§63), the one exception (`transfer_breaks_kinv`). -/
theorem kstep_preserves {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hdd : DDSound k) (hinv : KInv s)
    (h : KStep k s s') : KInv s' ∨ ∃ src dst, TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') := by
  obtain ⟨op, hop⟩ := kstep_iff.1 h
  cases op with
  | transfer src dst => exact .inr ⟨src, dst, hop⟩
  | _ => exact .inl (op_preserves hdd hinv hop fun _ _ e => KernelOp.noConfusion e)

/-- Every kernel step preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (§40, §49.7) from a state satisfying `KInv`
(§57) and `KAux`. -/
theorem kstep_preserves_kAux {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hinv : KInv s) (haux : KAux s)
    (h : KStep k s s') : KAux s' := by
  obtain ⟨op, hop⟩ := kstep_iff.1 h
  exact op_preserves_kAux hinv haux hop

/-! ## `HeldAnchored` is preserved by every step (§44, §65, §63) -/

/-- From a state satisfying `KInv` (§57) and `HeldAnchored` (auxiliary) under `DDSound` (§80),
the steps of `KStepDU` are exactly the kernel steps whose resulting state satisfies `KInv`: the
restriction of `ReachableDU` keeps exactly the runs along which §57 holds. -/
theorem kstepDU_iff {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hdd : DDSound k) (hinv : KInv s)
    (hheld : HeldAnchored s) : KStepDU k s s' ↔ KStep k s s' ∧ KInv s' := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨op, hop, hdu⟩
    exact ⟨kstep_iff.2 ⟨op, hop⟩, (op_preserves_of_dst_usable hdd hinv hheld hop hdu).1⟩
  · rintro ⟨h, hk⟩
    obtain ⟨op, hop⟩ := kstep_iff.1 h
    refine ⟨op, hop, fun src dst e => ?_⟩
    subst e
    exact transfer_dst_usable_of_noDangling hinv.1 hop hk.2.1.2.2

/-- A state of `ReachableDU` is reachable (§57). -/
theorem ReachableDU.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3}
    (h : ReachableDU k statics s) : Reachable k statics s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨op, hop, -⟩ := h
    exact .step ih (kstep_iff.2 ⟨op, hop⟩)

/-- The main invariant of §57 (`WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan`, with `KAux` and
`HeldAnchored`) on the states reached by runs whose transfers keep the destination usable, under
`DDSound` (§80) and well-formed statics (`StaticsOK`, a hypothesis not stated by §47). The
restriction of the runs is not a clause of §63: without it the statement is false
(`reachable_kinv_false`). -/
theorem reachableDU_kinv {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} (hdd : DDSound k)
    (hst : StaticsOK statics) (h : ReachableDU k statics s) :
    KInv s ∧ KAux s ∧ HeldAnchored s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact init_kinv hst
  | step _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨op, hop, hdu⟩ := h
    have h' := op_preserves_of_dst_usable hdd ih.1 ih.2.2 hop hdu
    exact ⟨h'.1, op_preserves_kAux ih.1 ih.2.1 hop, h'.2⟩

/-- Outcome relation of a kernel operation (§58, §60–§75): the step relation of the operation. -/
def KernelOp.Step (k : K) : KernelOp → S3 → Outcome3 S3 → Prop
  | .derive src region m => DeriveStep src region m
  | .split src rs => SplitStep k src rs
  | .release a => ReleaseStep a
  | .transfer src dst => TransferStep k src dst
  | .depend q x => DependStep q x
  | .enter ps ls => EnterStep ps ls
  | .exit => ExitStep k
  | .read a ls => Read3Step a ls
  | .write a ls => Write3Step a ls
  | .writeShared a ls => WriteSharedStep k a ls
  | .pin p => PinStep p
  | .unpin p => UnpinStep k p
  | .endUse p => EndUseStep k p
  | .free p auth => FreeStep k p auth
  | .alloc pr ow ls => AllocStep k pr ow ls
  | .store a p => StoreStep a p

/-- A kernel step is the `ok` outcome of some operation O1–O16 (§57, §58). -/
theorem kstep_iff {k : K} {s s' : S3} : KStep k s s' ↔ ∃ op : KernelOp, op.Step k s (.ok s') := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    cases h with
    | derive h => exact ⟨.derive _ _ _, h⟩
    | split h => exact ⟨.split _ _, h⟩
    | release h => exact ⟨.release _, h⟩
    | transfer h => exact ⟨.transfer _ _, h⟩
    | depend h => exact ⟨.depend _ _, h⟩
    | enter h => exact ⟨.enter _ _, h⟩
    | exit h => exact ⟨.exit, h⟩
    | read h => exact ⟨.read _ _, h⟩
    | write h => exact ⟨.write _ _, h⟩
    | writeShared h => exact ⟨.writeShared _ _, h⟩
    | pin h => exact ⟨.pin _, h⟩
    | unpin h => exact ⟨.unpin _, h⟩
    | endUse h => exact ⟨.endUse _, h⟩
    | free h => exact ⟨.free _ _, h⟩
    | alloc h => exact ⟨.alloc _ _ _, h⟩
    | store h => exact ⟨.store _ _, h⟩
  · rintro ⟨op, h⟩
    cases op with
    | derive => exact .derive h
    | split => exact .split h
    | release => exact .release h
    | transfer => exact .transfer h
    | depend => exact .depend h
    | enter => exact .enter h
    | exit => exact .exit h
    | read => exact .read h
    | write => exact .write h
    | writeShared => exact .writeShared h
    | pin => exact .pin h
    | unpin => exact .unpin h
    | endUse => exact .endUse h
    | free => exact .free h
    | alloc => exact .alloc h
    | store => exact .store h

/-- Finite runs of kernel steps from `s` (§57): the reflexive-transitive closure of `KStep`. -/
inductive KStar (k : K) (s : S3) : S3 → Prop where
  /-- The empty run (§57). -/
  | refl : KStar k s s
  /-- A run followed by one kernel step (§57). -/
  | tail {t u : S3} : KStar k s t → KStep k t u → KStar k s u

/-- The reachable states of §57 are the states reached from `S3.init statics` by a finite run of
kernel steps. -/
theorem reachable_iff {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} :
    Reachable k statics s ↔ KStar k (S3.init statics) s := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    induction h with
    | init => exact .refl
    | step _ h ih => exact .tail ih h
  · intro h
    induction h with
    | refl => exact .init
    | tail _ h ih => exact .step ih h

/-! ## Outcomes (§58) and the base frame (§39) -/

/-- Only `alloc` may produce `fail` among O1–O16 (§58). -/
theorem op_fail_only_alloc {k : K} {op : KernelOp} {s : S3} (h : op.Step k s .fail) :
    ∃ pr ow ls, op = .alloc pr ow ls := by
  cases op with
  | alloc pr ow ls => exact ⟨pr, ow, ls, rfl⟩
  | _ => exact (Alloc.guarded_ne_fail h).elim

/-- No kernel step changes the bottom of the frame stack (§39: the base frame never exits). -/
theorem kstep_base {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : KStep k s s') : s'.F.getLast? = s.F.getLast? := by
  cases h with
  | derive h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | split h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | release h =>
    rename_i a
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    unfold releaseEff; split <;> rfl
  | transfer h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | depend h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | enter h => exact enter_keeps_base h
  | exit h => exact (exit_keeps_base h).2
  | read h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | write h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | writeShared h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | pin h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | unpin h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | endUse h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | free h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | alloc h => cases h with | ok => rfl
  | store h =>
    rename_i a p
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    unfold storeEff; split <;> rfl

/-- On every reachable state, the bottom of the stack is the base frame 0 (§39, §47). -/
theorem reachable_base {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} (h : Reachable k statics s) :
    s.F.getLast? = some 0 := by
  induction h with
  | init => rfl
  | step _ h ih => rw [kstep_base h]; exact ih

/-- In every `ok` step, a leaf that becomes `Init` is written by the step (§59): a permitted write
(`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already

theorem init_only_by_writes {k : K} {op : KernelOp} {s s' : S3} {l : Nat}
    (h : op.Step k s (.ok s')) (hl : s.I l ≠ .init) (hl' : s'.I l = .init) : op.Writes s l := by
  cases op with
  | derive => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact absurd hl' hl
  | split => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact absurd hl' hl
  | release a =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    unfold releaseEff at hl'; split at hl' <;> exact absurd hl' hl
  | transfer src dst =>
    obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    have e : (transferEff s src dst).I l = if l ∈ footprint s.P dst then .init
        else if l ∈ footprint s.P src then .moved else s.I l := rfl
    rw [e] at hl'
    split at hl'
    · rename_i hld
      obtain ⟨hlP, hleaf, hlp⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hld
      obtain ⟨r, hr, hrs, hc⟩ := hpre.sameShape.2 l (List.mem_range.2 hlP) hlp
      have h1 := hpre.sameShape.1 r hr hrs
      rw [hc] at h1
      have hkr : kids s.P r = [] := by
        have : (kids s.P l).length = 0 := by rw [kids_nil_iff.2 hleaf]; rfl
        exact List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by simp only [OptP] at h1; omega)
      have hrf : r ∈ footprint s.P src :=
        mem_footprint.2 ⟨List.mem_range.1 hr, kids_nil_iff.1 hkr, hrs⟩
      exact ⟨hld, r, hrf, hc, hpre.srcInit r hrf⟩
    · split at hl'
      · cases hl'
      · exact absurd hl' hl
  | depend => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact absurd hl' hl
  | enter ps ls =>

    rw [e] at hl'; split at hl'

    · exact absurd hl' hl

    · assumption
    · exact absurd hl' hl

  | unpin => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact absurd hl' hl
  | endUse p =>

    rw [e] at hl'; split at hl'
    · cases hl'
    · exact absurd hl' hl

/-- Every `Init` leaf of a state reached by a run from `S3.init statics` was declared `Init`
(§47) or was made `Init` by a write step of that run (§59): a step `t → t'` of the run, through
an operation writing the leaf, after which the run continues from `t'` to the final state. -/
theorem init_history {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} {l : Nat}
    (h : KStar k (S3.init statics) s) (hl : s.I l = .init) :
    (∃ e, statics[l]? = some e ∧ e.2 = true) ∨
      ∃ (t t' : S3) (op : KernelOp), KStar k (S3.init statics) t ∧ op.Step k t (.ok t') ∧
        t.I l ≠ .init ∧ t'.I l = .init ∧ op.Writes t l ∧ KStar k t' s := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact .inl ((init_statics statics l).1 hl)
  | tail ht hst ih =>
    rename_i t u
    by_cases htl : t.I l = .init
    · rcases ih htl with hd | ⟨t₀, t₀', op, h₀, hs₀, hn₀, hi₀, hw₀, h₀'⟩
      · exact .inl hd
      · exact .inr ⟨t₀, t₀', op, h₀, hs₀, hn₀, hi₀, hw₀, .tail h₀' hst⟩
    · obtain ⟨op, hop⟩ := kstep_iff.1 hst
      exact .inr ⟨t, u, op, ht, hop, htl, hl, init_only_by_writes hop htl hl, .refl⟩

/-- Every library step, with or without the guard of §56, preserves the library invariant (§55),
when the kernel state before satisfies `WF3` and the one after `NoDangling` (§57). -/
theorem lInv_stepNG {k : K} {L L' : LState} (h : LStepNG k L L') (hw : WF3 L.kern)
    (hnd : NoDangling L'.kern) (hi : LInv L) : LInv L' := by
  cases h with
  | kernel hk => exact lInv_kernel hk hw hnd hi
  | newArena hb => exact lInv_newArena hb hi
  | issue hs => exact lInv_issue hs hi
  | reset hs => exact lInv_reset hs hi

/-- Conditional `ArenaInv` (§55) on library runs with or without the guard of §56: every live
entry of a reachable library state satisfies `EntryInv`, **provided** every kernel-reachable state
satisfies `WF3` and `NoDangling` (`hK`). `hK` is part of the main-invariant claim of §57, which is
false as stated (`Access.reachable_kinv_false`, the §63 ownership cycle). At `(K0, st)`, the
instance of every witness of this file, both `hK` (`Witness.lReach_inv_hyp_false`) and the
conclusion (`Witness.lReach_inv_conclusion_false`, `Witness.arenaInv_broken_by_transfer`) are
false. This theorem is therefore a conditional, not a proof that `ArenaInv` is preserved on
library runs. Only `lInv_newArena`, `lInv_issue` and `lInv_reset` hold with no kernel
hypothesis; `lInv_kernel` and `lInv_stepNG` take the per-step instances of `hK` (`WF3` before,
`NoDangling` after), which the breaking `transfer` of `Witness.arenaInv_broken_by_transfer`
violates. -/
theorem lReachNG_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics}
    (hK : ∀ s, Reachable k statics s → WF3 s ∧ NoDangling s) {L : LState}
    (h : LReachNG k statics L) : LInv L := by
  induction h with
  | init => intro E hE; cases hE
  | step hL hs ih => exact lInv_stepNG hs (hK _ hL.reachable).1 (hK _ (hL.step hs).reachable).2 ih

/-- Conditional `ArenaInv` (§55) on library-reachable states: every live entry satisfies
`ArenaInv`, **provided** every kernel-reachable state satisfies `WF3` and `NoDangling` (`hK`, part
of the §57 claim, false as stated: `Access.reachable_kinv_false`). At `(K0, st)` both `hK` and
the conclusion are false (`Witness.lReach_inv_hyp_false`, `Witness.lReach_inv_conclusion_false`):
an accepted `transfer` (§63) makes the storage of a live arena unusable
(`Witness.arenaInv_broken_by_transfer`). A conditional only (see `lReachNG_inv`). -/

  fun E hE hl => ((lReachNG_inv hK h.ng E hE).2 hl).1

/-- `arena_reuse_safe` (§78, §86): after a legal `reset`, along every continuation of the library
run, no authority that was derived from `internal` and covered a recycled leaf, previously issued
blocks included, is active again, so none is exercisable: no access to it is possible. -/
theorem arena_reuse_safe {k : K} {L L₁ L₂ : LState} {i : Nat} {E : ArenaEntry}
    (hE : L.arenas[i]? = some E) (hr : ResetD i L (.ok L₁)) (hrun : LRun k L₁ L₂) {j : Nat}
    (hj : E.internal ∈ L.kern.ancs j) (hc : ∃ l ∈ L.kern.afp j, l ∈ footprint L.kern.P E.storage) :
    ¬ L₂.kern.Active j ∧ ∀ m, ¬ L₂.kern.ExercisableAt j m := by
  have h1 := reset_ends_covering hE hr hj hc
  have hnot : ¬ L₂.kern.Active j := fun ha => by
    by_cases hjl : j < L₁.kern.A.length
    · exact h1 (hrun.akeep.active_back ha hjl)
    · obtain ⟨y, hy, -⟩ := ha
      obtain ⟨l, hl, -⟩ := hc
      have hjL : j < L.kern.A.length := by
        cases hlj : L.kern.A[j]? with
        | none => simp [S3.afp, hlj] at hl
        | some _ => exact lt_of_getElem? hlj
      exact hjl ((lstep_akeep (k := k) (.reset hr)).lt hjL)
  refine ⟨hnot, fun m hx => hnot ?_⟩
  cases hx with
  | base hy ha => exact ⟨_, hy, ha⟩
  | held hy ha => exact ⟨_, hy, ha⟩

def ptrAddr (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (a : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  match (s3.afp a).filter (fun l => decide (0 < (L l).len)) with
  | l :: ls => some (minOver (leafAddr s2 L) (leafAddr s2 L l) ls)
  | [] => if s3.afp a = [] then some (baseOf s2 (anchorAlloc L s3 a)) else none

/-- The region of authority `a` is empty or has a leaf of nonzero size: the domain where the
the address rules recorded for §82.3 define the address of a reference. -/
def PtrDecided (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (a : Nat) : Prop :=
  s3.afp a = [] ∨ ∃ l ∈ s3.afp a, 0 < (L l).len

/-- Decidability of `PtrDecided` (§82.3). -/
instance (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (a : Nat) : Decidable (PtrDecided L s3 a) := by
  unfold PtrDecided; infer_instance

/-- The address of a reference is defined exactly on `PtrDecided` (§82.3). -/
theorem ptrAddr_isSome {s2 : Machine.State} {L : Layout} {s3 : S3} {a : Nat}
    (h : PtrDecided L s3 a) : ∃ ad, ptrAddr s2 L s3 a = some ad := by
  unfold ptrAddr
  split
  · exact ⟨_, rfl⟩
  · rename_i he
...
    mem_footprint.2 ⟨hpre.usable.lt, hpre.leaf, hpre.usable.lt, .inl rfl⟩⟩

/-- Realization of `store` (§82 preamble, §82.3, §65, §16): under `Repr`, `WF3`, an `ok` step of
`store(authority, target)` whose region has a reference address (`PtrDecided`, address rules)
and the parametric obligations of the write, the write of the reference into the range of
`target` is an `ok` raw step, and `Repr` holds after the step. `PtrDecided` is not a clause of
the spec: it excludes the nonempty regions whose leaves all have size zero, for which no address
rule is recorded (§82.3 fixes no address). -/
theorem r6_store {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {ty : Nat → Ty} {pe : PtrEnc} {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat}
    {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} {a p : Nat} (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3)
    (h : StoreStep a p s3 (.ok s3')) (hpd : PtrDecided L s3 a)
    (hob : OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (storeOps pe s2 L ty s3 a p)) :
    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (storeOps pe s2 L ty s3 a p) s2 (run s2 (storeOps pe s2 L ty s3 a p)) ∧
      Repr L rtok s3' (run s2 (storeOps pe s2 L ty s3 a p)) := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨ad, had⟩ := ptrAddr_isSome (s2 := s2) hpd
  simp only [storeOps, had] at hob ⊢
  refine writes_repr hR hw (fun l hl => by rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hl]; exact store_target hpre)
    hob ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ <;> unfold storeEff <;> split
  · rfl
...
  | .free p auth, _, _ => freeOps π.L p auth
  | .alloc _ _ ls, s3, s2 => allocOps π.pl π.geom π.rtok s3.P.length s2 (rootIdx ls.toShape)
  | .store a p, s3, s2 => storeOps π.pe s2 π.L π.ty s3 a p
  | _, _, _ => []

/-- Obligations of one step (§20.3, §82): the parametric obligations of its reads and writes; the
layout of new places (`enterFrame`, `alloc`, §82.1); the instantiation of `K.FreeCompat` (`free`,
§80, §82.4); a reference address defined by the address rules (`store`, §82.3; not a clause of
the spec, see `r6_store`). -/
def StepObl {Ty : Type} (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty)
    (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) (π : Params Ty) (op : KOp) (s3 : S3) (s2 : Machine.State) :
    Prop :=
  OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2) ∧
    match op with
    | .enter _ ls => NewLayout π.L (enterP s3 ls) s3.P.length s2.next π.geom (rootIdx ls.toShape)
    | .alloc _ ow ls => NewLayout π.L (allocP s3 ow ls) s3.P.length s2.next π.geom
        (rootIdx ls.toShape)
    | .free p auth => k.FreeCompat p auth → FreeCompatInst C π.rtok p auth
    | .store a _ => PtrDecided π.L s3 a
    | _ => True

/-- Realization of every kernel step (§82 preamble, R6): under the obligations of the parameters,
`Repr`, `WF3` and `NoDangling` (parts of the kernel invariant `KInv`, §57) and the obligations of
the step, the raw operations of the step form an execution of `ok` raw steps, and `Repr` holds
after the step. -/
theorem r6 {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {π : Params Ty} {op : KOp} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State}
    (hπ : ParamsOK C π) (hR : Repr π.L π.rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3) (hnd : NoDangling s3)
    (h : OpStep k op s3 s3') (hob : StepObl k C ObR ObW π op s3 s2) :
    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (opsOf π op s3 s2) s2 (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2)) ∧
      Repr π.L π.rtok s3' (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2)) := by
  obtain ⟨hpl, hg, htc⟩ := hπ
  obtain ⟨hob, hx⟩ := hob
  cases op with
  | derive => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_derive hR h⟩
  | split => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_split hR h⟩
  | release => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_release hR h⟩
  | transfer => exact r6_transfer hR hw h hob
  | depend => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_depend hR h⟩
  | enter => exact r6_enter hR hw h hpl hg hx
  | exit =>
    have := r6_exit (ObR := ObR) (ObW := ObW) hR hw h htc
    exact ⟨this.1, this.2.2⟩
  | read =>
    have := r6_read (C := C) hR hw h hob
    exact ⟨this.1, this.2.2⟩
  | write => exact r2_write hR hw h hob
  | writeShared => exact r2_writeShared hR hw h hob
  | pin => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_pin hR h⟩
  | unpin => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_unpin hR h⟩
  | endUse => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_endUse hR h⟩
  | free =>
    have := r6_free (ObR := ObR) (ObW := ObW) hR hw hnd h hx
    exact ⟨this.1, this.2.2⟩
  | alloc => exact (r6_alloc hR hw h hpl hg hx).2
  | store => exact r6_store hR hw h hx hob

/-! ## Simulation (§82 preamble) -/

/-- Runs of the kernel from `S3.init statics` translated into the memory machine, with the
contract `K`, the deallocation compatibility `C`, the obligations `ObR`, `ObW` and the parameters
`π` fixed once for the run (§20.3 ¶3, §82): the initial state with the creations and writes of the
statics (`repr_init`); then each `ok` kernel step from a state satisfying `WF3` and `NoDangling`
(parts of the kernel invariant, §57) under its obligations, followed by its raw operations. The
invariant is a hypothesis on the states of the run, not a consequence of reachability, since
`transfer` can break it (an ownership cycle, §63 against §49.8 and §54). -/
inductive SimRun {Ty : Type} (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty)
    (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) (statics : Statics) (π : Params Ty) :
    S3 → Machine.State → Prop where
  | init : StaticsOK statics →
      NewLayout π.L (S3.init statics).P 0 0 π.geom (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))) →
      OblAlong ObR ObW (run Machine.State.empty (allocOps (Ty := Ty) π.pl π.geom π.rtok 0
        Machine.State.empty (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))))) (writeOps (run Machine.State.empty
          (allocOps (Ty := Ty) π.pl π.geom π.rtok 0 Machine.State.empty
            (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))))) π.L π.ty π.ival (initLeaves statics)) →
      SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π (S3.init statics)
        (run Machine.State.empty (initOps π.pl π.geom π.rtok π.L π.ty π.ival statics))
  | step {op : KOp} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} : SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π s3 s2 →
      WF3 s3 → NoDangling s3 → OpStep k op s3 s3' → StepObl k C ObR ObW π op s3 s2 →
      SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π s3' (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2))

/-- Simulation (§82 preamble, §57, §9 ¶9): for every translated run, the memory state is reached
from the empty state by an execution of `ok` raw steps, it is related to the kernel state by
`Repr` (admissibility included), and the kernel state is reachable from `S3.init statics` by the
kernel steps O1–O16. -/
theorem simulation {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {statics : Statics} {π : Params Ty} {s3 : S3}
    {s2 : Machine.State} (hπ : ParamsOK C π) (h : SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π s3 s2) :
    (∃ ops, Machine.Exec C ObR ObW ops Machine.State.empty s2) ∧ Repr π.L π.rtok s3 s2 ∧
      Access.Reachable k statics s3 := by
  induction h with
  | init hst hlay hob =>
    obtain ⟨hex, hR⟩ := repr_init (C := C) hst hπ.1 hπ.2.1 hlay hob
    exact ⟨⟨_, hex⟩, hR, .init⟩
  | step _ hw hnd hs hob ih =>
    obtain ⟨⟨ops, hex⟩, hR, hr⟩ := ih
    obtain ⟨hex', hR'⟩ := r6 hπ hR hw hnd hs hob
    exact ⟨⟨_, exec_append hex hex'⟩, hR', .step hr hs.kstep⟩

/-! ## Pinned addresses (§82.6, §74, §75) -/

/-- The automatic storage deallocated by `exitFrame` dies with the frame (§73): every place of
`exitRoots` is usable before the exit and not after. -/
theorem exitRoots_dies {s3 : S3} (hw : WF3 s3) (hF : s3.F ≠ []) {r : Nat}
    (hr : r ∈ exitRoots s3) :
    s3.Usable r ∧ ¬ ({ s3 with F := s3.F.tail } : S3).Usable r := by

(srun K0 (· = ·) obR obW πU (sinit [] πU) opsU).getD (sinit [] πU)

/-- Every step of the run passes its checks (§49, §54, §60–§75, §82). -/
theorem runU_ok : (srun K0 (· = ·) obR obW πU (sinit [] πU) opsU).isSome = true := by decide

/-- **A reachable `store` outside the address rules** (gap of the address rules recorded for
§82.3; §71.1, §65). The run is translated with `Repr` (so the layout satisfies `LayoutWF`), its
final kernel state is reachable and satisfies `WF3` and `NoDangling`, and `store(4, 2)` is an `ok`
kernel step from it (§65); `split` then `store` is how the derived `issue` is realized (Part
XIV). The region of 4 is `[3]`,
nonempty, and its only leaf has size zero: `PtrDecided` fails, `ptrAddr` is undefined, and the
obligations of the step (`StepObl`) do not hold, so neither `r6_store` nor `SimRun` covers this
step (`arena_issue` and `LSimRun` require the same `PtrDecided` for the `store` of an `issue`). -/
theorem store_zero_size_undecided :
    ((∃ os, Machine.Exec (· = ·) obR obW os Machine.State.empty finU.2) ∧
      Repr πU.L πU.rtok finU.1 finU.2 ∧ Access.Reachable K0 [] finU.1) ∧
    LayoutWF πU.L finU.1 finU.2 ∧ ParamsOK (· = ·) πU ∧ WF3 finU.1 ∧ NoDangling finU.1 ∧
    StoreStep 4 2 finU.1 (.ok (storeEff finU.1 4 2)) ∧ finU.1.afp 4 = [3] ∧ (πU.L 3).len = 0 ∧
    ¬ PtrDecided πU.L finU.1 4 ∧ ptrAddr finU.2 πU.L finU.1 4 = none ∧
    ¬ StepObl K0 (· = ·) obR obW πU (.store 4 2) finU.1 finU.2 := by
  have h := sim_of (piOf_ok _ [3]) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) runU_ok
  have hpd : ¬ PtrDecided πU.L finU.1 4 := by decide
  exact ⟨h, h.2.1.layout, piOf_ok _ [3], wf3_of_check (by decide), noDangling_of_check (by decide),
    .ok (by decide), by decide, by decide, hpd, by decide, fun hob => hpd hob.2⟩

end Runs

## 82. Representation Relation and Concrete Obligations

1. **Places and bytes:** relate `P`, `footprint` leaves, their ownership, and their parts to the storage units, offsets, ranges, identities, and alignment constraints of the elementary memory machine; establish actual disjointness for `DeclaredDisjoint` declarations.
2. **Authorities and operations:** connect effective modes and `ExercisableAt` to concrete read, write, and pointer-validity conditions; show that safe access governed by Parts VI through XV satisfies the obligations of Part III, without conflating ownership and binary representation.
3. **Initialization:** relate `Uninit`, `Init`, and `Moved` to concrete values and representations; an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into **a single logical leaf** with an appropriate representation.
4. **Allocation and deallocation:** relate `alloc` / `free` to `AllocStep` / `DeallocStep`, justify `Satisfiable`, `Deallocable`, and `FreeCompat`, as well as the zero-physical-size case.
5. **Lifetimes:** relate `endUse`, `exitFrame`, `NoDangling`, dependencies, and death markers to the validity effects on actual storage.
6. **Pinning and static storage:** prove compatibility of permitted moves and pinned-address restrictions; specify the physical obligations of statics and external use. Hardware-specific MMIO semantics remain outside the sequential kernel.
7. **Arenas:** show that the library abstraction's derived operations and metadata, distinct from `S₃`, can be realized by operations O1–O16; relate issued regions and local/static/allocated storage to the elementary memory machine without reintroducing access after invalidation.
8. **`noalias`:** infer no pointer-lowering property from abstract invariants alone; memory justification is established here and the translation choices at Spec 13 level.

# XVIII. Examples of Semantic Behavior

The fragments below are **traces of abstract operations**, not language syntax. The judgments illustrate normative rules; they create no exception to the detailed preconditions.

## 83. Address Reuse and Old Provenance

An allocation `a` is created and an access retains its provenance; after deallocation, a new allocation `b` may occupy the same address. `a ≠ b` as abstract identities: reading through the old access is invalid even if the addresses are equal. A new valid access with provenance `b` may be used within its rights.

∀ (a b : Nat) (sa sb : Slot), pl.slots[a]? = some sa → pl.slots[b]? = some sb → a ≠ b →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P sa.place, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sb.place

/-- `PoolInv`, item 3, the transition guarantee, as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex,
D.4: "`freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot
concerné"; non-normative library contract): `freeSlot` never succeeds while an active strict
descendant of a companion covers the slot concerned (§43, §69). The contract does not restrict the
companion to the pool of the slot. This guarantee is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false`): D.3 exempts "`internal` et ses ancêtres", which
may include a companion of another pool. -/
def FreeGuarantee (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- Same-pool restriction of the transition guarantee (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3;
non-normative library contract). This is not the contract's statement (`FreeGuarantee`): only the
companions of the slot's pool are quantified (`r.pool = pl.id`). On that point it is weaker; it also
covers the companion itself, and on that point it is stronger (§43, §69). -/
def FreeGuaranteeSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, r.pool = pl.id → ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → (x = r.comp ∨ r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x) →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- `PoolInv` as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, as corrected; non-normative
library contract): entry disjointness, `pool_no_stale_access`, and the transition guarantee of
`freeSlot` (§55, §57). It is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
def PoolInv (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop := EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuarantee k L

/-- Same-pool restriction of `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library
contract): items 1 and 2 as the contract states them, item 3 restricted to the companions of the
slot's pool (`FreeGuaranteeSamePool`). This is not the contract's statement (`PoolInv`) (§55,
§57). -/
def PoolInvSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L

/-- `EntriesDisjoint` follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1)
(§40). -/
theorem entriesDisjoint_of {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) : EntriesDisjoint L := by
  intro pl hpl
  have hok := hwf.pools _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hpl)
  exact ⟨fun sl hsl l hl => hok.slotIn sl.place (List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.place)) hsl) l hl,
    fun a b sa sb ha hb hab => hok.disjoint a b sa.place sb.place
      (by simp [Pool.shape, ha]) (by simp [Pool.shape, hb]) hab⟩

/-- The same-pool transition guarantee follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4
annex, D.4, item 3, restricted to the slot's pool): an active descendant of a companion of the pool
is younger than `internal`, so it is neither `internal` nor one of its ancestors, and
`ContentEndPre` forbids it to cover the entry (§43, §69). -/
theorem freeGuaranteeSamePool_of {k : K} {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) :
    FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L := by
  intro j h L' hst pl sl hpj hsl r hr hrp x hx hxr l hl hlq
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl' sl' hpj' _ _ hsl' hpre =>
    rw [hpj] at hpj'; cases hpj'
    rw [hsl] at hsl'; cases hsl'
    obtain ⟨hint, hlt, -, -⟩ := res_internal hwf hr (List.mem_of_getElem? hpj) hrp
    obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := hx
    have hex := hpre.entry x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ ⟨l, hl, hlq⟩
    have hcx : r.comp ≤ x := by
      rcases hxr with rfl | hc
      · exact Nat.le_refl _
      · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hc)
    unfold Exempt at hex
    rcases hex with rfl | h'
    · omega
    · have := chain_lt h'; omega

/-- `pool_inv_preserved`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4): `PoolInvSamePool`
holds on every state of a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57); with
`PReach.toI`, on every library-reachable state under the guarantee of §57. This is not the
contract's statement: `PoolInv` is false on such a state (`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
theorem pool_inv_preserved_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : PoolInvSamePool k L :=
  have ⟨_, hwf, hns, _⟩ := pReachI_inv h
  ⟨entriesDisjoint_of hwf, hns, freeGuaranteeSamePool_of hwf⟩

/-- `pool_entries_disjoint` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1; §40). -/
theorem pool_entries_disjoint {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    EntriesDisjoint L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).1

/-- `pool_no_stale_access` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 2): on every state of a library run
(`PReachI`), an active entry authority designates a live slot at its current generation (§89). -/
theorem pool_no_stale_access {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    NoStale L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.1

/-- `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3):
on every state of a library run (`PReachI`), `freeSlot` never succeeds while the companion of a
resolution of the pool, or an active descendant of it, covers the slot (§43, §69). This is not the
contract's statement: `FreeGuarantee` is false on such a state
(`Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false`). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.2

/-- Exclusivity of a `Modify` companion, as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2:
"Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool";
non-normative library contract): an active `Modify` companion of a pool is the only active
companion that covers a leaf of that pool's storage (§43, §50). The contract does not restrict the
other companions to the same pool. This property is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false`). -/
def ModifyExclusive (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, ∀ pl ∈ L.pools, r₁.pool = pl.id → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
    L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify →
    (∃ l ∈ L.kern.afp r₂.comp, l ∈ footprint L.kern.P pl.storage) → r₁.comp = r₂.comp

/-- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "La
propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau"): on every state
of a library run (`PReachI`), whatever its kernel steps, an active `Modify` companion of a pool is
the only active companion of that pool (§43, §50). This is not the contract's statement:
`ModifyExclusive`, which also covers the companions of other pools, is false on such a state
(`Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false`). -/
theorem pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
      L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify → r₁.comp = r₂.comp := by
  intro r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp ha₁ ha₂ hm
  refine Decidable.byContradiction fun hne => ?_
  have := (pReachI_inv h).2.2.2 r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp hne ha₁ ha₂
  rw [hm] at this; cases this.1

/-- One `ok` step of a library run (HandlePool v0.4 annex; non-normative library contract): a
kernel step O1–O16 of non-administrative code, the registry unchanged, or an accepted pool
operation (§57, §58). -/
inductive PStep (k : K) : PState → PState → Prop where
  | kernel {L : PState} {s' : S3} : KStep k L.kern s' → PStep k L { L with kern := s' }
  | newPool {L L' : PState} {others : List (List Nat)} {st i : Nat} :
      NewPoolStep others st i L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | allocSlot {L L' : PState} {j dst : Nat} : AllocSlotStep j dst L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | resolve {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} {m : Mode} :
      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | resolveMany {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {hs : List Handle} {m : Mode} :
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | unresolve {L L' : PState} {c : Nat} : UnresolveStep c L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | freeSlot {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
      PStep k L L'

/-- Library states reachable from the initial library state (§47) by library steps (HandlePool v0.4
annex; non-normative library contract). -/
inductive PReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PState → Prop where
  | init : PReach k statics (PState.init statics)
  | step {L L' : PState} : PReach k statics L → PStep k L L' → PReach k statics L'

/-- Library runs in which every step starts from a kernel state satisfying `KInv` (§57; HandlePool
v0.4 annex). Under the guarantee of §57 every library-reachable state is such a state
(`PReach.toI`); the pool theorems are stated on these runs, so that they do not depend on that
guarantee. -/
inductive PReachI (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PState → Prop where
  | init : PReachI k statics (PState.init statics)
  | step {L L' : PState} : PReachI k statics L → KInv L.kern → PStep k L L' →
      PReachI k statics L'

/-- Kernel side of library runs (§57, §69 effect; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): a kernel step
O1–O16, or the end of the content of a slot place `q` under `ContentEndPre` for some `internal`
`i`. -/
inductive XStep (k : K) : S3 → S3 → Prop where
  | kernel {s s' : S3} : KStep k s s' → XStep k s s'
  | contentEnd {s : S3} {q i : Nat} : ContentEndPre k s q i → XStep k s (endUseEff s q)

/-- States reachable from `S3.init statics` by `XStep` (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
inductive XReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : S3 → Prop where
  | init : XReach k statics (S3.init statics)

theorem XReach.kseq {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s s' : S3} (hr : XReach k statics s)
    (h : KSeq k s s') : XReach k statics s' := by
  induction h with

  | tail _ hs ih => exact .step ih (.kernel hs)

/-- The guarantee of §57 on the kernel side of library runs (HandlePool v0.4 annex): `KInv` on
every state reached by kernel steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents. It is not a clause of the
contract and is not proved here: `xreach_inv` reduces it to the preservation of `KInv ∧ KAux` by
every kernel step, which the transfer of §63 breaks (`transfer_breaks_kinv`). -/
def KernelGuarantee (k : K) (statics : Statics) : Prop := ∀ s, XReach k statics s → KInv s

/-- A library step from a kernel state in `XReach` lands in `XReach`, under `KInv` (§57;
HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem xreach_pstep {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L L' : PState}
    (hr : XReach k statics L.kern) (hk : KInv L.kern) (hs : PStep k L L') :
    XReach k statics L'.kern := by
  rcases pstep_kernel hk hs with h | ⟨q, i, hpre, he⟩
  · exact hr.kseq h
  · rw [he]; exact .step hr (.contentEnd hpre)

/-- The kernel state of every library-reachable state is reached from `S3.init statics` by kernel
steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex), given `KInv` on such
states. -/
theorem pReach_xreach {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hX : KernelGuarantee k statics)
    {L : PState} (h : PReach k statics L) : XReach k statics L.kern := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ hs ih => exact xreach_pstep ih (hX _ ih) hs

/-- `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57) holds on every state reached by kernel steps and ends of slot contents,
when it holds initially and every kernel step O1–O16 preserves it (`contentEnd_preserves` covers the
ends of slot contents; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
theorem xreach_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics}
    (h0 : KInv (S3.init statics) ∧ KAux (S3.init statics))
    (hK : ∀ s s', KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → KInv s' ∧ KAux s') {s : S3}
    (h : XReach k statics s) : KInv s ∧ KAux s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact h0
  | step _ hs ih =>
    cases hs with
    | kernel hs => exact hK _ _ ih.1 ih.2 hs
    | contentEnd hpre => exact contentEnd_preserves ih.1 ih.2 hpre

theorem optP_false_iff {α : Type} {o : Option α} {P : α → Prop} :
    OptP o P False ↔ ∃ y, o = some y ∧ P y := by
  cases o with
  | none => simp [OptP]
  | some y => simp [OptP]

/-- The replaced element belongs to the list (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: pool updates; §46). -/
theorem mem_set_self' {α : Type} : ∀ {l : List α} {i : Nat} {a x : α}, l[i]? = some a →
    x ∈ l.set i x
  | [], _, _, _, h => by simp at h
  | _ :: _, 0, _, _, _ => by simp

687:# Annexe D — Instance `HandlePool` (non normative, contrat de bibliothèque)
691:## D.1 — Identité, état et stockage
697:## D.2 — Emprunt composé et résolution
707:## D.3 — Allocation et fin d'usage de slot
715:## D.4 — Invariant corrigé et limites
717:`PoolInv` exige : (1) les entrées sont deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; (2) aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`) ; (3) **garantie de transition** : `freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné. La dernière clause concerne le succès des transitions, non une interdiction globale de toutes les dérivations du noyau sur des slots libres. Les dérivations ordinaires issues d'une autorité d'entrée restent permises par le noyau.

# Annexe D — Instance `HandlePool` (non normative, contrat de bibliothèque)

Cette annexe décrit une **instance de bibliothèque** de la discipline MM-03, et non une nouvelle opération primitive du langage. Les noms sont sémantiques. Le contrat doit être reconstruit et vérifié ; les résultats du jalon 3 concernent le modèle exploratoire et ses conditions, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées ci-dessous.

## D.1 — Identité, état et stockage

Un handle est une donnée `(poolId, slot, gen)` **sans autorité d'accès intrinsèque**. L'identité logique `poolId` est fraîche et n'est pas réutilisée pendant l'exécution pertinente : détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle. Chaque pool vivant conserve une entrée abstraite `{storage, internal, slots}`, où chaque slot possède `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`. Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage` ; leur métadonnée abstraite est représentée en octets par l'implémentation de bibliothèque.

`storage` peut être local, statique, alloué ou être un bloc issu d'une arène. **`newPool(storage, internal)` exige que toutes les feuilles du stockage d'entrée soient `Uninit`** et doit vérifier la garde unifiée de MM-03.3 §2.7 bis sur les deux registres des abstractions vivantes. Il reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena` sans fabriquer ni droits ni initialisation des valeurs de slots. Les entrées libres sont `Uninit` ; leur génération initiale est zéro. Une autorité ne peut être `internal` de deux abstractions vivantes, et une arène ne peut réutiliser l'`internal` d'un pool vivant.

## D.2 — Emprunt composé et résolution

Une résolution réussie dérive **de `internal` une autorité compagne** couvrant toutes les feuilles du stockage du pool, de mode `Observe` ou `Modify`, puis dérive **de cette compagne** une autorité de même mode par entrée résolue. L'autorité d'entrée est une descendante de la compagne, et non une autre dérivation indépendante de `internal`. Les deux sont soumises aux règles ordinaires de modes effectifs, d'exercice, de détention, d'ancrage et de transfert ; aucune permission nouvelle n'est créée.

`resolve(h, Observe | Modify)` vérifie l'identité de pool, la génération et la vivacité du slot **avant toute création d'autorité** : handle d'un autre pool, périmé, slot absent ou libre ⇒ `fail`, sans changement d'état. Une résolution valide exige l'exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis. Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool ; des compagnes `Observe` peuvent coexister. Il est impossible de libérer une compagne tant que ses descendantes d'entrée sont actives (O3.2). La propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau, pas seulement deux appels successifs de `resolve`.

`resolveMany(handles, Modify)` crée **une** compagne `Modify` et une autorité `Modify` par entrée. La distinction des slots est vérifiée dynamiquement pour ce lot ; toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**, sans création partielle de droits. `resolveMany(handles, Observe)` utilise des dérivations `Observe` de la compagne `Observe`, **sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction** : la répétition du même handle valide est permise. Les `reject` de discipline d'accès restent distincts des `fail` de validation des handles.

`unresolve` libère d'abord toutes les dérivées d'entrée encore actives, puis la compagne. Les règles de `release`, y compris celles qui empêchent la libération en présence de descendants ou d'ancres valides, restent applicables ; le contrat ne supprime pas silencieusement des autorités transférées.

## D.3 — Allocation et fin d'usage de slot

`allocSlot(pool, dst)` exige un pool vivant, l'autorisation d'administration de ses métadonnées, une destination utilisable et libre d'autorité active, non `Init`, apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle. `fail` si aucun slot libre ; `ok` choisit un slot libre, le rend vivant, conserve sa génération et écrit son handle dans la seule feuille `dst`, selon les obligations de représentation (Spec 4) et d'ABI (Spec 11). **Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit`** jusqu'à son écriture ; l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot.

`freeSlot(h)` exige un pool **vivant** et `MetaRight`, c'est-à-dire le droit légal d'administration de la valeur pool par `Modify` exerçable ou par mutation `writeShared` admissible de ses métadonnées `SharedMutable`. `fail` si l'identité ou la génération ne correspond pas ; un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité. Pour réussir, la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible : **aucune dépendance utilisable** ne serait invalidée, **aucune feuille n'est épinglée**, et **aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres**. En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée. Le contrôle n'interprète pas `internal` comme un emprunt externe empêchant systématiquement le nettoyage de ses propres slots.

L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`, remet les feuilles de l'entrée à `Uninit`, marque l'entrée libre et incrémente sa génération ; **il ne désalloue pas implicitement l'allocation MM-02 du stockage**. Il ne s'agit pas de supposer une invocation de O12 autorisée par simple `MetaRight` : la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**, notamment dans les cas `writeShared`.

## D.4 — Invariant corrigé et limites

`PoolInv` exige : (1) les entrées sont deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; (2) aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`) ; (3) **garantie de transition** : `freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné. La dernière clause concerne le succès des transitions, non une interdiction globale de toutes les dérivations du noyau sur des slots libres. Les dérivations ordinaires issues d'une autorité d'entrée restent permises par le noyau.

Les générations sont des entiers naturels dans le modèle abstrait. Leur débordement ou leur recyclage dans une représentation finie doivent être empêchés par l'implémentation (par exemple retrait définitif d'un slot) ; l'ABI est spécifiée en Spec 11. L'encapsulation qui empêche un client d'accéder directement à une compagne administrative appartient à la Spec 9. Les handles persistants peuvent représenter des liens cycliques ; les résolutions qui en découlent restent temporaires et soumises à MM-03.

**Statut des preuves :** le jalon 3 rapporte `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, `pool_no_stale_access`, `pool_resolveMany_atomic`, `pool_resolveMany_distinct`, `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` et `pool_entries_disjoint` sur son brouillon, sous les hypothèses détaillées dans `J3_v0.1.md`. Il rapporte également un contre-exemple à l'ancienne formulation de `pool_inv_preserved`. **Il ne constitue pas encore la preuve** de la nouvelle règle `freeSlot` sous `MetaRight` ni de la totalité du contrat corrigé : ces obligations sont consignées en annexe F.

registry. -/
def PState.init (statics : Statics) : PState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0, []⟩

/-- The pool read as an arena entry with nothing available or issued, to reuse `MetaRight` of §36
(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library contract). -/
def Pool.entry (pl : Pool) : Arena.ArenaEntry := ⟨pl.storage, pl.internal, [], []⟩

/-- Administrative right on the pool (§36; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, corrected by §36;
non-normative library contract): the pool is live (`internal` active) and `MetaRight` holds,
exercisable `Modify` over the pool value; no `writeShared` branch. -/
def AdminRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Prop := s.Active pl.internal ∧ Arena.MetaRight s pl.entry

/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Decidable (AdminRight s pl) := by
  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance

/-- Place of slot `i`, `0` if absent (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative library
contract; §46). -/
def slotPlace (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((pl.slots[i]?).map (·.place)).getD 0

/-- The pool with slot `i` replaced (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library
contract; §46). -/
def setSlot (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : Pool := { pl with slots := pl.slots.set i sl }

/-! ## `newPool` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §56) -/

/-- The pool registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1;
non-normative library contract): the `internal` identities of its live pools. -/
def liveInternals (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) : List Nat :=
  (pools.filter fun pl => decide (s.Active pl.internal)).map (·.internal)

/-- Preconditions of `newPool(storage, internal)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative
library contract; §56, §76). -/
structure NewPoolPre (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) (others : List (List Nat))
    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- D.1: "reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena`" (§76.1–§76.3, §76.5). -/
  base : Arena.NewArenaBase s storage internal
  /-- D.1: every leaf of the input storage is `Uninit`. -/
  uninit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, s.I l = .uninit
  /-- D.1, §56: `internal` is absent from the pool registry and from every other registry of live
  administrations `others`. -/
  guard : Arena.Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal

/-- Decidability of `NewPoolPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §56, §76). -/
instance (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
    Decidable (NewPoolPre s pools others storage internal) :=

/-- Decidability of `HandleOK` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §89). -/
instance (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Decidable (HandleOK pl h) := by
  unfold HandleOK; infer_instance

/-- Legal exercise of `internal` at mode `m` for the companion (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2;
non-normative library contract): the preconditions of the `derive` of the companion from
`internal` over all leaves of the storage (§60). -/
def ResolveRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
  DerivePre s pl.internal (footprint s.P pl.storage) m

/-- Decidability of `ResolveRight` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Decidable (ResolveRight s pl m) := by
  unfold ResolveRight; infer_instance

/-- State after the companion (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60 effect; non-normative library
contract): authority `|A|`, derived from `internal` at mode `m` over all leaves of the storage. -/
def compS (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
      fun l hl => by rw [heff l hl]; exact Arena.allows_some_modify _⟩⟩

/-- An accepted `freeSlot` preserves the kernel invariant `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex,
HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constitue une obligation
explicite"). -/
theorem freeSlot_preserves {k : K} {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} (hk : KInv L.kern)
    (ha : KAux L.kern) (hst : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L')) : KInv L'.kern ∧ KAux L'.kern := by
  obtain ⟨pl, sl, -, -, -, -, hpre, he, -⟩ := pool_freeSlot_ends_content hst
  rw [he]; exact contentEnd_preserves hk ha hpre

/-- `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` under the `Modify` right (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): on a state
of a library run (`PReachI`) satisfying `KInv` (§57), an accepted `freeSlot` acts on a usable slot
over which the current frame has exercisable `Modify` through `internal` (§69.1), and leaves the
slot usable (§69: "`place` remains usable"; D.3: no deallocation). -/

A classical proof of totality is not a runtime requirement." Alternative: client-supplied identity with a "never assigned" precondition. No verdict changes on admissible states (`WF` makes the precondition true). Outside the domain `AllocStep` may be `ok` on a non-`WF` state, as §9 ¶10 allows.

"Absence of an intervening write or invalidation" (§16 ¶5).** Used (`Op.KeepsAlloc`): every intervening operation is a read, a creation, a deallocation of another identity, or a write through another provenance. Alternative: no intervening write at all. The hypothesis used is weaker, so `write_read_sub` is stronger; no verdict changes. `ops = []` gives the immediately following read.

Used: absolute half-open address ranges `[ac.addr, ac.addr + ac.len)` and `[ac'.addr, ac'.addr + ac'.len)` disjoint (`RangeDisjoint`, §9 ¶3); "result of a valid read" compared for `ok` reads before and after with the same obligations and type. effective anchor; provenance that allocation. Obtained: the same; the case passes. R5 is reached

the expected verdict: a decision of the brief recorded for §82.3 (empty-region rule), not stated
by spec v0 (§81 leaves encodings to Spec 11). -/

/-- Run of H16 as the kernel can run it (§70, §73): the callee frees the storage through its
parameter on `x`, then returns. -/
def h16o : List Op := h16p ++ [.free 3 7, .exit]
/-- State reached by `h16o` (§57). -/
def h16 : LState := final KF3 [] h16o

/-- **H16** (material §1 C, class N3). The callee receives by transfer a value owning a storage,
frees it, returns the value; the caller reads that storage. Expected (material): `ok`, then
`reject`. Obtained: the reception, `transfer` of `x` into the callee's local, is `reject`: the
parameter 4 is an active derived authority covering `x` held outside it (§63.4, §45). With the
storage freed through the parameter on `x` (`ok`) and the return (`ok`), the caller's read of the
storage is `reject` for every authority (§66.1: the leaf belongs to no usable place, §70 effect).
Twin without the `free`: the read is `ok`. **MISMATCH** on the reception (expected `ok`, obtained
`reject`); cause: case defect, the reception by value is a calling convention deferred to Spec 3
(§45, §81) and the literal kernel `transfer` is rejected by §63.4. -/
theorem H16 : RunsTo KF3 [] h16p h16a ∧ TransferStep KF3 1 4 h16a.kern .reject ∧
    ActiveDerivedOutside h16a.kern 1 4 ∧ RunsTo KF3 [] h16o h16 ∧
    (∀ a, Read3Step a [3] h16.kern .reject) ∧ Runs KF3 [] (h16p ++ [.exit, .read 3 [3]]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), by decide, runsTo (by decide),
    read_rejected (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Test contract of H17 (§70.2, §80): the storage 4 and the region leaf 5 deallocable by the
authority 7, so that only the structural clause can reject. -/
def h21o : List Op := h21p ++ [.derive 0 [0] .observe, .derive 2 [2] .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf],
  .writeShared 4 [0]]
/-- State reached by `h21o` (§57). -/
def h21 : LState := final KA [] h21o

/-- **H21** (material §1 D, class Lib). A callee that only observes the arena issues a block to a
local, then returns the block. Expected (material): `ok`. Obtained: the `writeShared` on the
metadata is `ok` (§68), but the `issue` is `reject`: `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` on
the arena value and `writeShared` alone does not satisfy it (§36, §77.1). Twin, the same run with a
`Modify` parameter on the arena value: `issue`, `transfer` of the block value to the caller and
`exitFrame` are `ok`. **MISMATCH** (expected `ok`, obtained `reject`); cause: spec change (§36,
§77.1). -/
theorem H21 : RunsTo KA [] h21o h21 ∧ IssueD KA 0 [4] 6 h21 .reject ∧
    OptP (h21.arenas[0]?) (fun E => ¬ MetaRight h21.kern E) False ∧
    Runs KA [] (h21p ++ [.derive 0 [0] .modify, .derive 2 [2] .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf],
      .writeShared 4 [0], .issue 0 [4] 6, .transfer 6 2, .exit]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (o := .issue 0 [4] 6) (by decide), by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of H21b (§72, §60, §65, §76): frame 1 with the result 0 passes 1, `Modify` on it, to
frame 2, which has the arena value 1 and the local buffer 2 (parts 3, 4); the callee derives 4,
`Modify` on the buffer, stores it into the arena value and creates the arena. -/

import Ern.Lib.HandlePool
import Ern.Lib.DataStack
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! (a) `KernelGuarantee` is false for `K0` and the statics of `transfer_breaks_kinv`,
although `K0` satisfies `DDSound`. -/

theorem reach_xreach {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} (h : Reachable k statics s) :
    Ern.Lib.HandlePool.XReach k statics s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ hs ih => exact .step ih (.kernel hs)

theorem not_kernelGuarantee :
    DDSound Examples.K0 ∧ ¬ Ern.Lib.HandlePool.KernelGuarantee Examples.K0 TransferWitness.cycStatics := by
  obtain ⟨hdd, s, s', hr, -, -, ht, hn⟩ := transfer_breaks_kinv
  exact ⟨hdd, fun hX => hn (hX s' (.step (reach_xreach hr) (.kernel (.transfer ht))))⟩

/-! (b) Dead pool: a handle whose pool identity is that of a pool no longer live gives `reject`
(only outcome), not `fail`, although the handle passes `HandleOK`. -/
namespace DeadPool
open Ern.Lib.HandlePool Ern.Lib.HandlePool.Witness Examples

def wd : PState := { w4 with kern := releaseEff w4.kern 3 }

theorem wd_reach : PReachI K0 hst wd :=
  .step w4_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.kernel (.release (Guarded.ok (by decide))))

theorem dead_pool_rejects :
    PReachI K0 hst wd ∧ wd.pools[0]? = some pl4 ∧ ¬ wd.kern.Active 3 ∧ HandleOK pl4 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ ∧
    ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .observe wd .reject ∧
    (∀ o, ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .observe wd o → o = .reject) := by
  refine ⟨wd_reach, by decide, by decide, by decide, .noRight (pl := pl4) (by decide) (by decide),
    fun o ho => ?_⟩
  cases ho with
  | noPool h => rfl
  | noRight => rfl
  | fail hp hR =>
    have e : wd.pools[0]? = some pl4 := by decide
    rw [e] at hp; cases hp; exact absurd hR (by decide)
  | noEntry => rfl
  | ok hp hR =>
    have e : wd.pools[0]? = some pl4 := by decide
    rw [e] at hp; cases hp; exact absurd hR (by decide)
end DeadPool

/-! (c) DataStack R7: after a transfer of the block value, `grow` stores the grown block into the
recorded (moved-from) destination, not where the block value now is. -/
      by decide, by decide⟩⟩
end FreeNotKernel

#print axioms FreeNotKernel.free_outside_kernel

/-- The step hypothesis `hK` of `xreach_inv` is false for `K0`. -/
theorem xreach_inv_hK_false :
    ¬ ∀ s s', KInv s → KAux s → KStep Examples.K0 s s' → KInv s' ∧ KAux s' := by
  intro hK
  obtain ⟨-, s, s', -, hk, ha, ht, hn⟩ := transfer_breaks_kinv
  exact hn (hK s s' hk ha (.transfer ht)).1

/-! ## Library runs in the memory machine (§82 preamble, §82.7) -/

/-- Library runs from `LState.init statics` translated into the memory machine, with the contract
`K`, the deallocation compatibility `C`, the obligations `ObR`, `ObW` and the parameters `π` fixed
once for the run (§20.3 ¶3, §82, §82.7): the initial state with the creations and writes of the
statics (as `SimRun.init`); then each `ok` library step, kernel steps and arena operations
interleaved, from a library state whose kernel state satisfies `WF3` and `NoDangling` (parts of
the kernel invariant, §57, as in `SimRun`), under the obligations of its kernel steps, followed by
the raw operations of its kernel steps. -/
inductive LSimRun {Ty : Type} (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty)
    (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) (statics : Statics) (π : Params Ty) :
    LState → Machine.State → Prop where
  | init : StaticsOK statics →
      NewLayout π.L (S3.init statics).P 0 0 π.geom (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))) →
      OblAlong ObR ObW (run Machine.State.empty (allocOps (Ty := Ty) π.pl π.geom π.rtok 0
        Machine.State.empty (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))))) (writeOps (run Machine.State.empty
          (allocOps (Ty := Ty) π.pl π.geom π.rtok 0 Machine.State.empty
            (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))))) π.L π.ty π.ival (initLeaves statics)) →
      LSimRun k C ObR ObW statics π (LState.init statics) (minit π statics)
  | step {lop : LOp} {L L' : LState} {s2 : Machine.State} : LSimRun k C ObR ObW statics π L s2 →
      WF3 L.kern → NoDangling L.kern → LOpStep k lop L L' → KObl k C ObR ObW π (kexp lop L) s2 →
      LSimRun k C ObR ObW statics π L' (run s2 (lopsOf π lop L s2))

/-- A kernel simulation run extends along a kernel sequence whose steps start from states
satisfying `WF3` and `NoDangling`, under their obligations (§82 preamble). -/
theorem simRun_path {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {statics : Statics} {π : Params Ty} {s3 s3' : S3}
    {t : List (KOp × S3)} (hp : KPath k s3 t s3') :
    ∀ {s2 : Machine.State}, SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π s3 s2 →
      (∀ q ∈ t, WF3 q.2 ∧ NoDangling q.2) → KObl k C ObR ObW π t s2 →

/-- R1, R2, R4, R6 for the derived `issue` of entry `i` (§77, Part XIV, §82.2, §82.3, §82.5,
§82.7). Under `Repr` and `WF3`, for an `ok` issue, when the block's region has a reference address
(`PtrDecided`, not a clause of the spec, see `r6_store`) and the parametric obligations of the
write hold: `split` realizes no raw operation and `store` realizes exactly one raw write, of the
range of the destination, with the bytes of the reference to the block (address `ad`, provenance
the allocation of its effective anchor); no read (R1); the write is an `ok` raw step (R2) and
`Repr` holds after it (R6); `LiveCover` (R4) is kept, the new block included. -/
theorem arena_issue {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {π : Params Ty} {L L' : LState} {i : Nat}
    {region : List Nat} {dst : Nat} {E : ArenaEntry} {s2 : Machine.State}
    (hE : L.arenas[i]? = some E) (hR : Refinement.Repr π.L π.rtok L.kern s2) (hw : WF3 L.kern)
    (hs : IssueD k i region dst L (.ok L'))
    (hpd : PtrDecided π.L (splitEff L.kern E.internal [region]) L.kern.A.length)
    (hob : OblAlong ObR ObW s2
      (storeOps π.pe s2 π.L π.ty (splitEff L.kern E.internal [region]) L.kern.A.length dst)) :
  obtain ⟨hex, hR, -⟩ := simulation hπ h.simRun
  exact ⟨hex, hR, h.lreach⟩

/-- R4 along library runs (§82.5, §54): in every state of a translated library run whose kernel
state satisfies `WF3` and `NoDangling`, every leaf covered by an active authority has a live
allocation containing its range. -/
theorem lsim_r4 {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {statics : Statics} {π : Params Ty} {L : LState}
    {s2 : Machine.State} (hπ : ParamsOK C π) (h : LSimRun k C ObR ObW statics π L s2)
    (hw : WF3 L.kern) (hnd : NoDangling L.kern) : LiveCover π.L L.kern s2 :=
  liveCover_of (lsimulation hπ h).2.1 hw hnd
